$comment: The layout system the console and the desktop panel share. Both repos carry this file; each repo's gate asserts its own stylesheet uses these numbers AND that this file's sha256 matches the literal recorded in the other repo's test. Change it in both repos or neither.

page.$comment: The page BODY: one column, one inset, one rhythm (the sixty-second and sixty-ninth lists). `gap` is 24 on EVERY page of both surfaces. **AND THE RHYTHM BELONGS TO THE CONTAINER THAT HAS LIKE THINGS IN IT (the sixty-ninth list):** a LIST declares its own tick (`listGap`, the card's own 8) on ITS OWN element, never on the page root. Measured before: `page-plugins` put the card's 8 on the page root, so that page's head sat 8 px off its first block while Memory's sat 24 (144 → 168); and Settings charged the frame's 24 AND a `margin-bottom: 12` for the same separation, which is 36 — a value on no surface's scale (2/4/6/8/10/12/14/16/24). A separation declared twice is not a separation twice as clear; it is a number nobody chose. **AND `max` IS THE BOX, NOT THE CONTENTS (the seventieth list):** the console draws `width: min(1120px, 100%)` under a global `* { box-sizing: border-box }`, so its page is 1,120 WIDE with 1,072 of contents; the panel declared `max-width: 1120px` with no reset, so its page was 1,168 wide with 1,120 of contents — the same contract number meaning two different measurements, 48 px apart. Below `wide` that 48 was not free: measured at 390/639/767/1088 the panel's page box was 48 wider than the pane holding it and stuck 31 px past the window's right edge, where the console was never wider than its parent. `boxSizing` is recorded here so the next frame reads one arithmetic. **AND ITS INSET IS A STEP AT THE PHONE BAND (the hundred-and-ninth list).** Measured 2026-11-11 across fifteen widths: the console drew `24px/24px/24px/24px` from 1,600 down to **360**, so a 390 px phone spent **12%** of its window on chrome while the panel — which steps at 639 — spent **21%**. Two frames, one page. **The step is the same one the scale already had** (`space.scale` has no 24 below the desk, and `--sp-3-5` is 14): at or below `breakpoints.phone` the page's inset is `phonePad`, on BOTH surfaces.

ground.$comment: The surface every page sits ON, which both draw (the fifty-fourth list). ONE colour per theme — no gradient, because a wash behind a page is decoration carrying no information, and rule 17 refuses it. Measured: the panel carried three decorative gradients behind a fixed overlay plus a fourth on its canvas, in six hand-written colours, while the console painted one.

palette.$comment: The greys, and the two rules about them (the fifty-sixth list). `ink` and `muted` were already identical on both surfaces; the THIRD grey was not — `#696a74` on the console and `#6f707a` on the panel, six apart on one channel and identical on the others, two names for a colour the eye cannot tell from the other. A palette is: ink, muted, faint, one accent, and the semantic four. Anything else is a decision that has to be made in the open. **AND A WASH IS A TOKEN TOO (the sixty-sixth list):** the panel's three badges took their ink from tokens and their backgrounds from literals (`rgba(40,160,80,.18)`, `rgba(220,60,60,.18)`, `rgba(200,160,40,.18)`), so one control had two sources of colour; a fourth hue (`rgba(90,130,240,.15)` / `#7aa2ff`) and a fifth green (`#30d158` beside `--success #2f9e44`) were colours no scale declared. **AND THE HUES A PAGE MAY PAINT ARE ENUMERABLE (the hundred-and-sixth list).** Measured 2026-11-11 as a census: the panel's Terminal page painted **nine** warm colours for one accent, and the memory page a **teal** the palette had no name for. The accent family is now written down with its distances in CIE76 (accent→solid 6.6, accent→on-soft 9.2, accent→ink 9.2 — all under the ~10 a reader can name apart, which is why each member earns its place by a MEASURED contrast job rather than by taste), and `extraHues` records the one non-semantic hue the product deliberately draws: the memory tag's teal, whose ink must clear AA on its own wash.

accentFamily.note: each job exists for a measured contrast need: brand 5.49 white, wall 6.08 white at button size, wallHover 6.78 (a hover that DARKENS), textOnWash 6.95 (a label on the wash), ink 3:1 for graphics; the console's brand doubles as its graphic ink, which is why its `ink` slot is the accent itself **AND THE JOB WITH NO TOKEN WAS FILLED WITH THE WRONG ONE (the hundred-and-twenty-fourth list).** Measured 2026-11-11: the console painted accent TEXT on the wash with `--accent` — **4.93:1** on `#fff0e6` — while the panel used `--accent-on-soft #9c3a0a` at **6.2:1**. **Both pass AA, so nothing was broken**: the defect is TWO ANSWERS to one job, and this atom recorded the console's member as `(none)`. It is `--accent-on-soft` on both surfaces now, **declared in both blocks**, because after dark the wash is a dark brown and the light value measures **1.4:1** while the dark accent measures **7.07:1** — a member is a JOB and its value is the theme's.

extraHues.name: tag
extraHues.reason: the memory tag's chips; a hue the semantic four cannot carry, and it reads on its own wash

space.$comment: The rhythm, and the two ways a number that is not on it can still be right (the fifty-ninth list). A rhythm is a scale: **2/4/6/8/10/12/14/16/24** — the steps BOTH surfaces declare; the console has a 32 step the panel does not, and the contract records the shared ladder rather than the union, because a step one surface cannot reach is not a rhythm they share. A painting value OFF it is a nudge UNLESS it measures something else: a CONTROL's height (5 + 5 + an 18 px line box = 28) or the padding inside a FIXED target (1 px inside a 24 px box). Those are named tokens, so an editor who changes a line-height cannot silently change a control's height. **AND A TARGET HAS TWO NUMBERS, ONE PER INPUT DEVICE (the seventy-sixth list).** `target` (24) is the smallest box a MOUSE can be aimed at, and it is what this scale's controls are built to. A THUMB needs 44: measured 2026-11-10 at 390 px wide, the console had **0 of 127** controls under 44 across its three pages (one `@media (max-width: 639px)` block naming `main`'s controls, written in the twenty-ninth list) while the panel had **11 of 11** — a 27 px field, 22 px buttons and 24 px doors. 44 is not on the spacing scale and does not need to be: it is a TARGET, like `target` itself — a box that must be hit, not a gap between boxes. The two numbers are recorded together because one name for both is how the thinner surface went unnoticed.

leading.$comment: Line-height, as THREE ratios rather than eight (the sixtieth list). Measured before: the console declared `1` (8x), `1.45` (7x), `1.5` (9x), `1.4` (3x), `1.2` (2x), `1.6`, `1.55` and `0`; the panel `1` (10x), `1.5` (6x), `1.55` (4x), `1.6` (3x), `1.45` (2x) and `1.3` — and on ONE rendered page the same 13 px text painted 19.5 px, 16.5 px and `normal`. A reader cannot see .05 of a ratio, so it was never a choice. `mark` is 1 and means a GLYPH IN A BOX (a dot, a chevron, a button's label inside a fixed control); a sentence may not take it.

measure.$comment: How wide a line of PROSE runs (the sixty-first list). Measured before: the panel's `.archive-row-item` ran to 103 characters and `.connect-where` to 109 while Memory's entries stopped at 66 and the console's prose at 46 — the same product asking a reader to move their eye 1,120 px on one page and 517 on another. A measure is not a taste: 66ch is where the block that already reads well sits, and it is inside the 45-75 band a line is followed back along. A CODE SNIPPET IS EXEMPT — scanned token by token, and wrapping it would break copy-paste — so this is a TOKEN a rule opts into, never a blanket.

hairline.$comment: The one family of SEPARATING lines, and the rule about state marks (the fifty-seventh list). A hairline separates two regions and takes `line`; a STATE MARK declares a state and takes its own colour (a pill's edge is its ink, so greyscale keeps its shape and its word). Measured before: the panel had THREE names for the first family — `--line` and `--chrome-line` were the same `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` written twice, and `--glass-hairline` was a COOL `rgba(24,32,54,.07)` for the same job on the same page. **AND A STATE MARK CARRIES A WORD, NOT ONLY A COLOUR (the sixty-eighth list):** the panel's rail mark cycles through all five liveness states and carried them in colour and shape only — its word lived in a `title`, which is a hover and not a surface — while its sibling `.plug-dot`s all have their state written beside them (`Loaded`, `Running`). The console was already right: `.fleet-status` says "offline · last seen …" and `.home-verdict` says "0 of 1 online · 1 needs attention". **AND A CENSUS MUST COUNT RULES, NOT ELEMENTS (the hundred-and-twenty-third list).** Measured 2026-11-11: a border census inside `.page` gave Home **32** against Activity's **4** and read as an 8x drift — **25 of Home's 32 were `td`/`th` bottom edges from ONE shared rule**, a table's row rule doing its grouping. **Counting an element and counting a rule are different questions**, so this atom names the three kinds a border can be: a `rowRule` (one per table), a `box` on a region, and a `box` on a control — and a page's count is only meaningful when it says which it is counting.
hairline.rowRule: a td/th edge: ONE rule per table, not one border per cell
hairline.box: a border on a region (card, fold, section) or on a control (input, button, tab)

regionBand.$comment: **A PAGE'S REGION BOXES MEASURED 3 TO 8 ON EVERY PAGE OF BOTH SURFACES (the hundred-and-twenty-third list).** Home 6 · Activity 3 · Settings 8 · Plugins 6 — 2026-11-11 at 1,440, boxes on REGIONS only (a table's row rule and a control's own edge excluded). **This is a measured band, not a taste:** a page that drew 23 REGION boxes would be outside it, and one that drew 23 CONTROL boxes would not be — because a control's edge is its affordance and its count is the page's form, which no scroll of this atom can decide.

head.$comment: The page's ONE head (the sixty-second list). Its height is its CONTENTS — the pages measured 68/68/33 px because one carries tabs and two carry a subtitle — so `height` is not a number. What IS recorded: the gap, the alignment, the subtitle SLOT (the second line of the title's block, `.page-sub`), and the rule that a page has ONE head — anything under it is a card. **AND THE TITLE'S BLOCK HAS TWO SLOTS, NOT ONE (the hundred-and-twenty-first list).** Measured 2026-11-11, rendered: a page under a title carries a **CLAIM** (the sentence the page exists to make — `3 of 4 online · 2 need attention`, `Today: 543 client calls`) and a **CONTEXT** (what the page is — `Connection, device limits and diagnostics for …`, `Following the console's audit as it is written.`). **The atom recorded only the context**, so each page put its claim wherever it liked: console Home **22/600**, console Activity **17/600**, and the panel **no claim at all** under a title that had one on Home. One page is not a layout; two slots are.

claimSlot.$comment: **THE CLAIM SLOT IS A POSITION, NOT ONE STEP (the hundred-and-twenty-first list).** Measured 2026-11-11: the sentence a page exists to make sat at the TITLE's rung on Home (`3 of 4 online · 2 need attention`, 22/600), at the SECTION's on Activity (`Today: 543 client calls`, 17/600), and NOWHERE on the panel (`Settings` went straight to its fold). **Home's being at the title's rung is a recorded decision and a gate pins it** (`the two pages must NOT converge`); what was missing is the record that a claim BELONGS in the head's block at all, and that its step is one of TWO — `xl` when it is the page's second title line, `lg` when the page's title is the whole claim. **A third step is a decision, not a choice.** **AND WHICH STEP TO TAKE IS A FIELD NOW, NOT A SENTENCE (the hundred-and-twenty-second list, item 2).** The choosing rule was prose in this comment — *`xl` when it is the page's second title line, `lg` when the page's title is the whole claim* — and **a comment cannot refuse an 18 px claim**. `stepBy` names the two conditions and the two answers, so a gate in each repo reads the same rule and a third step has to argue with it.

row.$comment: A ROW inside a list (the eighty-seventh list). Measured 2026-11-10 across both surfaces: seven row shapes for ONE idea — heights 36/46/57/76/77/134, insets `0`, `8px 10px`, `8px 12px`, `16px`, and the space AFTER a row 0/6/8/18. What is ONE decision is recorded here; what is a LEVEL is left to the page, because a memory entry IS taller than a plugin name. A list of LINES (the attention rows, the fleet table, the timeline) separates by its own leading and draws a rule only where the meaning changes; a list of BOXES separates by the scale's 6-8.

cardTitle.$comment: The card's TITLE, which both surfaces draw (the fifty-third list). Measured before: the panel's card header drew `h2` at 14/600 and the console's drew `<strong>` at 13/600 — the same visual role, two elements at two sizes, and on the console the element that LOOKED like the title was not one. `level` is the section above it (`section.h2` is 17), so the pair is a two-step ladder rather than two opinions.

elevation.$comment: The three LEVELS a shadow can mean, and which atoms may carry one (the fifty-fifth list). `flat` is a card ON the page — a hairline and a tint, no shadow. `pane` is a surface ABOVE it (a drawer, a modal, a popover) and is the only thing that floats. `raised` is a control lifted inside a pane (a segmented switch's active arm), a 1-2 px lift. Measured before: the panel's card carried a four-layer `--glass-shadow` while the console's carried `none`, so a card was two objects on the two surfaces. **AND THE PANE LEVEL IS ONE OBJECT (the hundred-and-eleventh list).** Measured 2026-11-11 with a popover OPEN on each surface: the console's `.machine-pop` floated on `rgba(0,0,0,.12) 0 12px 32px` (a one-layer drop), a **10 px** radius and a `.14` edge; the panel's `.session-menu` floated on a **two-layer** shadow (a wide drop AND a drawn `0 0 0 1px` ring), a **14 px** radius and a `.08` edge. **Two popovers, two objects** — and the token the atom named for this level was carried by NEITHER sheet. The pane is now `paneShadow` + `paneRadius` + `paneEdge`, written once and read by both. **AND A RECESSED BLOCK IS THE CARD'S STEP WITH THE SIGN REVERSED (the hundred-and-seventeenth list).** Measured 2026-11-11: every spelling of a recess in the light scale — `.settings-fold`'s `#fafafa`, the console's `--panel-3` `#f4f4f5`, `--surface-recessed: var(--bg)` — lands at **1.027 or 1.000** against the pane, because the scale's steps are 3–8 levels apart and **a usable recess needs 8 levels BELOW the pane** (`grey 239` = 1.074, the card's own 1.072 with the sign reversed). **So this is not a token to pick; it is a derivation to state.** The card is `color-mix(ink 3.5%, surface)`; the recess is `color-mix(ink 7%, surface)` in light, and after dark the card's direction reverses, so the recess is the mix toward the GROUND.
elevation.recess: the card's step, reversed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 7%, var(--surface)) light; toward the ground after dark

radius.$comment: The corner scale, and WHAT EACH STEP IS FOR (the fifty-eighth list). The rule is not the count but the MEANING: a page nests card -> row -> control -> mark, and each is one step; an overlay is drawn LARGER than the pane it covers, which is why its steps are bigger. Measured: `--radius-lg: 20px` is painted on NO page a person browses — the console uses it inside three overlays and the panel on one dialog — so the largest step is an OVERLAY step and is recorded as one. `row` (10) was the step neither side assigned: the panel's own comment called it "cards inside a pane" while painting it on `.btn` and `.tab`, and the console paints it on `.fleet-row` and `.tool-list`. A 40 px TARGET and a 24 px control are the same proportion, so they cannot share one value: `target` is its own step.

rail.$comment: Each surface's first column, and THE WIDTH EACH FORM STARTS AT (the seventy-fourth list). The CONSOLE has THREE: the LABELLED rail is 232 px from `tablet`+1 (768) up; the ICON rail is 56 px from `phone`+1 (640) through 767; below 640 the rail is the phone's bottom bar and the page's left is 0 — measured at 390/480/639. `consoleCollapsesAt` is 767, the last width at which the labelled rail is NOT drawn. **THE NUMBER WAS RIGHT AND THE STYLESHEET DID NOT OBEY IT.** Measured 2026-11-10: the icon band's rule `(min-width: 640px) and (max-width: 767px)` paints a 56 px rail, and TWO later `(min-width: 640px)` queries — one repainting `.shell`'s columns, one `.rail`'s width — overrode it on source order alone, so the labelled sidebar never collapsed: the rail measured **232** wide at 640/700/767, the page 408/468/535, and the fleet table (min-content 635 px inside `overflow: hidden`) lost four of its five columns with nothing to scroll. The contract test read the number and passed; the page read the CSS. The contract records the FORM's floor for that reason, and each repo's test now compares the NUMBER against the RULE rather than against a breakpoint it happens to equal. The PANEL never collapses: it is a device app in a window, and its rail is the page's first column at every width. The widths are recorded rather than equalized; the COLLAPSE is a rule, not a habit.

section.$comment: The levels UNDER a page title (the forty-ninth list). A page has one title and the blocks below it are a LEVEL, not a size chosen per page: `h2` is a section, `h3` is the thing inside one, `eyebrow` is the small uppercase label above a block. Measured before: an h2 was 22, 17, 14 or 10 px depending on the page. **AND ONE SIZE CAN CARRY TWO ROLES, SO THE ATOM NAMES WHAT SEPARATES THEM (the hundred-and-twenty-second list).** Measured 2026-11-11: **17/600 is the page's CLAIM on both surfaces, a DAY HEADING inside the record, and this atom's `h2`** — three roles, one step, and on Activity the claim (`Today: 543 client calls`) and a day (`Tuesday, 11/10`) weigh the same, 217 px apart. **There is no free step** between 22 and 17 to move the claim into (item 2 of this list), and the tracking differs by **0.34 px** — a difference the tracking atom's own comment calls invisible. **So the separator is not size: it is the SLOT.** A claim is in the page's HEAD; a day heading and an `h2` are in its BODY. A reader who cannot weigh two lines apart can still see which block they are in.

sameSizeDifferentRoles.$comment: One step, three roles. The marker that separates the claim is POSITION, not size or tracking.

label.$comment: A CONTROL's label (the sixty-fifth list). SENTENCE case, and the verb plus its subject — `Add a machine`, `New entry`, `Test the connection`, never a fragment with a glyph (`+ New`). ACRONYMS KEEP THEIR CAPITALS (`URL`, `AI`, `DSH`), which is the ONE exception and is listed rather than inferred: `Copy console URL` and `Connect an AI client` are both correct and a reader should not have to work out why. Measured: 21 of the console's 22 controls were already sentence case; `+ New` was the only fragment-with-a-glyph on either surface.

breakpoints.$comment: The widths where a page's SHAPE changes, and the FORM a query takes (the sixty-fourth list). A downward query ends at `N-1` and an upward one starts at `N`, so a breakpoint's two sides cannot both claim the same width — verified: the console's min set {640, 1088, 1280} and max set {480, 639, 767} do not intersect, and the panel's max set {639, 767, 1087} follows the same form. Measured before: the panel's approval banner used `(max-width: 1088px)` — AT the `columns` width — so it held its one-column shape one pixel into the wide band, which no eye can see and no author would feel.

empty.$comment: The EMPTY state's atom, which both surfaces draw (the forty-sixth list). A page with nothing to list shows one card, on the page's own grid: the card's corner and padding, start-aligned text, no shadow, and the full width of the page's column. It is NOT a dialog — a 20px corner, a drop shadow and centred text on a 1120px column is a modal drawn where a page's empty state belongs. **AND THE STATE KEEPS THE WAY BACK, AND THE CARD'S INSET IS ON THE CARD (the seventy-second list):** measured 2026-11-10 after filtering a list into nothing — the panel's was one 18 px line CENTRED in 1,042 px inside a `.card` whose inset came from the child's `margin: 14px` (so the card stood 48 px tall around one line), with NO control; the console's had the `Clear search` and no card. A reader who filtered a list into nothing needs the control that undoes it beside the sentence that explains it. **AND THERE ARE TWO SHAPES, NOT ONE (the hundred-and-thirteenth list).** A page whose whole body is empty draws `standalone`: a card of its own at the numbers above. An empty state INSIDE a card — a filtered table, a list panel — draws `inCard`: NO surface, NO radius, NO shadow (the thirty-eighth list's `no card inside a card`), the card's own inset, and **the atom's `gap`**, because the one thing the atom is FOR here is the distance between the sentence and the control that undoes it. Measured 2026-11-11: the console's `.audit-empty` drew `gap: 8` where every other empty in the product separates those two by **12**, and nothing in the atom said which shape it was.

shapes.standalone: a card of its own: the numbers above
shapes.inCard: no surface, no radius, no shadow; the card's inset and the atom's gap

failed.$comment: A failure's sentence NAMES THE SUBJECT, NOT THE TRANSPORT (the sixty-third list). Measured: the console's notice said "The console could not read the machine list" — the THING a person was waiting for — and the panel's said "tool memory_list failed", which names the RPC and leaves the reader to infer the page.

loading.$comment: The LOADING state's atom, which both surfaces draw (the forty-seventh list). A read that has not answered reserves the SHAPE of what it will draw: a card-sized skeleton row per item, with the read's own label in a live region. It is NOT a word in a result line: a loading state is not a result, and the count line is drawn only when it has a count.

motion.$comment: Rule 18's mechanism, recorded once for both surfaces (the fifty-second list). REDUCED MOTION IS A BLANKET: every transition and animation is capped at 0.01ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, because a NAMED LIST cannot cover a rule added later — measured, the panel still moved 4 elements at 0.2s under reduce while the console moved 0. The named list stays for the second half: an animation whose state must also stop (`animation: none`). `0.01ms` rather than `0s` so a `transitionend` listener still fires. **AND ITS DURATION IS ONE NUMBER (the hundred-and-fourth list).** Measured 2026-11-11 as a vocabulary: the console carried `background@0.12s` ×39 and the panel carried `@0.12s` ×12 PLUS `@0.2s`, `@0.15s` and `@0.06s` on its own rules, so the same hover was 0.12 s on one surface and 0.2 s on the other — and three speeds within one sheet. `interactionMs: 120` is the number both already used most; the panel's `--ds-transition-duration` family reads it, and a `transition` shorthand that writes its own duration is what the gate refuses.

tracking.$comment: RULE 14, AS A NUMBER: a size gets ONE step, and the step belongs to the SIZE (the seventy-fifth list). Measured 2026-11-10 by grouping every text node on a rendered page by its `font-size` (then by weight and by kind — an uppercase label, a mono value and prose are three kinds), and asking whether that group carried one `letter-spacing`: the console answered NO on every page (22 px at -0.242 AND -0.44, 12 px at -0.052 AND 0, 10 px at 0.5 AND 0, 17 px at -0.052 AND -0.34) while the panel answered YES. THE CAUSE WAS AN INHERITED BASELINE NO TOKEN NAMED: `body { letter-spacing: -0.004em }` reached every element, so 'the default' and '-0.004em' were two answers to one question depending on which element you inspected, and 19 rules opted INTO a token on top of it. After removing it every page of both surfaces answers YES: 22 px = display, 12 px = none, 10 px/label = label, 10 px/mono = none. THE STEPS ARE THE FOUR THE SHEETS ALREADY DECLARED and a caller reads one of them or none: display (-0.011em) for a title, nothing for body text, label (0.05em) for an uppercase label, eyebrow (0.08em) for the small word above a block. **`normal` is not a step** — a rule that writes it is answering a question the tokens already answer, and after this list not one rule on either surface does.

theme.$comment: WHICH SURFACE DECIDES THE THEME, AND HOW (the seventy-seventh list). Measured 2026-11-10 at 1,440 on both surfaces in one browser at one moment: with the OS dark the console's body was **rgb(19,20,24)** and the panel's was **rgb(250,250,250)** — two answers to one question, from one product. The console reads `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` and nothing else; the panel's `lib/theme.ts` returned `"light"` whenever nothing was stored and NEVER asked the OS, and its rail's switch flipped `body[data-theme]`. THE RULE, in two parts, because the two surfaces differ for a reason and only one of them is a defect: `decides` is SYSTEM on both — the first paint agrees with the reader's machine, because a device app is opened ON that machine and a web page beside it should not disagree. `override` is true on the panel and false on the console: a desktop app in a window may keep a cockpit theme while the OS is light, and the switch is how; a web page that overrode its OS would be the odd one, and the console has never offered it.

header.$comment: The frame's TOP ROW — the header that sits on the page body (the hundred-and-first list). It had no atom: the console drew a full-bleed RULE (52 px, opaque `--surface`, one hairline under it, no corner, no gap to the body) and the panel drew a rounded CARD (64 px, glass, a border on four sides, radius 14 = the DIALOG's corner, 8 px above the body). Neither was wrong alone — a desktop window's title bar versus a pane floating over a canvas — which is exactly the drift this contract exists to stop. THE DECISION: the header is a RULE that spans the surface's full width, 52 px tall, opaque, closed by ONE hairline, with NO corner and NO gap to the body it caps. A header is not a card: a card is a thing ON the page, and the header is the page's ceiling. The panel's canvas therefore stops insetting its top edge above the header, and the frame reads this record rather than its own habit.
